News.title: North Korea flaunts seized Western weapons in twisted Ukraine war museum as Kim vows to help Putin in ‘sacred’ invasion
News.content:
KIM Jong-un has flaunted destroyed Western weapons at a twisted museum opening – as he vowed to prop up Vladimir Putin in his “sacred” invasion of Ukraine.

The North Korean dictator has mercilessly thrown thousands of underprepared troops into Russia‘s meatgrinder, whom he honoured at the unveiling of a Pyongyang memorial.





Kremlin Defence Minister Andrey Belousov joined the Rocket Man as military jets flew overhead and white balloons were released into the air.

In his commemoration speech, Kim said Russia will “surely win a victory in the just sacred war” before reaffirming his support of the regime.

It is not known exactly how many North Korean soldiers have been sent to the frontline in Ukraine, but South Korean intelligence estimates that 15,000 were enlisted to help recapture parts of Kursk.

Seoul says that around 2,000 have been killed fighting alongside Russia, with many reported to have been sent on suicide missions through a snowy no-man’s land to soak up Ukrainian ammo.

Kim was yesterday seen shedding crocodile tears as he threw dirt over the remains of one dead soldier and lay flowers at the memorial of others.

Beloussov and Putin crony Vyacheslav Volodin were then reportedly left messages in a guest book honouring the fallen troops.

In a later speech, Kim said that the soldiers spirits will remain as a “symbol of the North Korean people’s heroism” and support “a victorious march by the Korean and Russian people”.

The despot also hailed the axis’ soldiers for thwarting a Western “hegemonic plot and military adventurism” in the war.



He did so in front Nato-supplied military vehicles – such as a Leopard 2A4, AMX-10, and M1117.

As well as troops, Pyongyang has supplied countless missiles and munitions to Moscow.

The Hermit Kingdom is worryingly believed to have received advanced weaponry – as well as much-need energy and food – from its bloodthirsty partner in return.

It is believed that Russia are bolstering North Korea’s fleet intercontinental ballistic missiles, military satellites, and conventional weapons systems.

Military cooperation between the star-crossed allies has grown since Kim and Putin signed a mutual defence treaty in Pyongyang in June 2024.



At the time, Kim hailed the treaty as the “strongest ever”.

After the memorial ceremony on Sunday, Kim met with Belousov and Volodin behind closed doors to discuss deepening those ties.

“We have reached an agreement with the DPRK defence ministry to place our military cooperation on a sustainable, long-term footing,” said Belousov.



“We are prepared to sign a Russian-Korean military cooperation plan for the 2027–2031 period this year.”

The projection of unity comes ahead of Donald Trump‘s summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing in May.

At the memorial ceremony, Volodin also read a letter from Putin, who wrote that the museum “will undoubtedly be a clear symbol of the friendship and solidarity” between the two countries.

The Russian dictator also lauded the “extraordinary bravery and genuine devotion” of the North Korean troops he sent blindly into gunfire.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Putin previously thanked Kim for greasing the wheels of his war machine at China’s military parade in Beijing last September.



He reportedly told Kim: “Your soldiers fought courageously and heroically.”

News.title: Donald Trump’s stoic reply when asked ‘why does this keep happening to you?’ after THIRD assassination attempt
News.content:
DONALD Trump coolly brushed off yet another attempt on his life – offering a blunt explanation when asked why he keeps being targeted.

The defiant US president was quizzed just hours after a gunman stormed a glitzy Washington dinner in the third assassination plot against him.





When asked bluntly, “Why do you think this keeps happening to you?”, Trump didn’t hesitate.

He said: “I must tell you the most impactful people, the people that do the most, you take a look at the people – Abraham Lincoln – I mean, you go through the people that have gone through this where they got ’em, but the people that do the most and the people that make the biggest impact are the ones that they go after.”

“Just take a look at the names here. The big names, and I hate to say I’m honored by that, but I’ve done a lot. We’ve done a lot,” he added.

Despite the repeated threats, Trump struck a confident tone.



“We’ve changed this country, and there are a lot of people that are not happy about that,” he said.

He also claimed his leadership transformed America from “a laughingstock” into “the hottest country in the world.”

And in a swipe at his critics, the president said attackers don’t go after people who “don’t do much because they like it that way.”

The latest horror unfolded at the high-profile White House Correspondents’ Dinner on Saturday night.



Suspected gunman Cole Thomas Allen allegedly burst into the Washington Hilton armed with a shotgun, handgun and knives.

Dramatic surveillance footage shows the black-clad suspect sprinting past stunned security guards toward the ballroom where Trump, top officials and thousands of journalists were gathered.

Within seconds, armed guards reacted and stopped the 31-year-old before he could reach his targets.



Police say Allen had rented a room inside the hotel and was heavily armed.

He was restrained without being shot and taken to hospital.

Trump later posted an image of the suspect lying face down on the carpet after the failed plot.

Before the attack, Allen sent a disturbing manifesto to family members, calling himself the “Friendly Federal Assassin”.

In the rambling message, he raged against the administration and chillingly outlined his plan.



Allen wrote: “I would still go through most everyone here to get to the targets if it were absolutely necessary… but I really hope it doesn’t come to that.”

His writings show he intended to target administration officials, and potentially Trump himself.

A relative alerted cops after receiving the message, but the warning came just minutes before the shooting began.

Investigators say Allen had a history of radical views and regularly trained with firearms.

This is now the third known attempt on Donald Trump’s life.



The first came in 2024 in Butler, Pennsylvania, when 20-year-old Thomas Matthew Crooks opened fire at a rally.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump was injured , and a supporter was tragically killed before Crooks was taken out by law enforcement.

Months later, a second plot emerged in Florida, led by 59-year-old Ryan Routh – who has since been sentenced to life in prison.

POLL OF THE DAY Is the King right to push ahead with State Visit after Trump dinner shooting? VOTE NOW

News.title: Crystal healer in bitter court battle with millionaire son who ‘exploited her guilt from divorce to pocket £2m’
News.content:
FAMILY AT WAR Crystal healer in bitter court battle with millionaire son who ‘exploited her guilt from divorce to pocket £2m’

A CRYSTAL healer is locked in a bitter court battle with her millionaire son after claiming he “exploited” her guilt from a divorce to pocket £2million.

Moya Montgomerie, 72, says “arch-manipulator” son, Jason Minns spent his adult life getting her to hand over vast sums in loans.





The mum claims he threatened to put her on the streets and said he would block her seeing her grandchildren.

Minns, 55, allegedly did all this while requesting cash to pay for his lifestyle and to invest in his property business.

Montgomerie has now taken her son to court after accusing him of “exploiting her guilt” for divorcing his dad and leaving him as a child to get the loans.

She is suing in a bid to get him to pay £1million she says she is owed, as well as to pay off the mortgage and sign over the deeds to her £1million home in Hampshire, which is in the names of Jason and his wife.



The reiki therapist, crystal healer and “angel card” reader says her son agreed to sign over the house in part-payment of his debts, but has gone back on the promise and declared he will “see her on the streets”.

But Minns and his wife Stephanie, 54, are fighting the case – with their lawyers claiming Montgomerie is a “serial liar” who owes him money.

He says most of the cash was a “gift” and that while he agreed to sell the “substantial” detached house to his mum and stepdad, he won’t do so until she stumps up £310,000 she allegedly owes him.

The court was told Montgomerie was brought up in “poverty” by her older brother after losing both of her parents by the time she was 12.



She went on to have her son when she was only 17, but her marriage to his dad did not last and they divorced in the 1980s, with Minns staying with his father.

Her barrister, Helen Brander, said: “Jason knows of Moya’s background and the guilt she feels from the divorce and that he remained with his father, although he spent time with his mother.

“Throughout his adult life, he has exploited that guilt for his financial gain.

“He has on many and varied occasions too numerous to particularise requested financial assistance from Moya by way of loans to assist with his and his wife’s costs of living and/or to use as liquid funds for investment…and Moya has on many and various occasions too numerous to particularise responded to those requests and has fulfilled them.”

Montgomerie said she loaned her son £600,000 by 2008 and then another £500,000 so he and Stephanie could pay off the mortgage on the house, which they used to live in prior to her moving in.



The mum claims when she has “queried” her son’s need for money, she has been “shouted at” and met with threats to cut her off from her grandchildren or to “turn her out” of the house and leave her “destitute.”

The property is in Minns and Stephanie’s names but Montgomerie claims an agreement was made to sign it over to her in exchange for her writing off £750,000 from the outstanding loans.

Despite that, they have since refused to sign it over and the mortgage on the property has not been paid off, the court heard.

But the couple’s lawyer Lauren Kreamer denies they have done anything wrong or that they owe the mum anything beyond £40,000 in loans, which should be balanced against what she owes them.

She says £500,000 was paid by Montgomerie towards a purchase price of £750,000 for the house, with £250,000 loaned to her by her son and daughter-in-law to cover the rest.



The court heard the couple are still owed the £250,000 loan, plus £60,000 interest, and £25,000 they have spent towards the outgoings on the house.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The case will go to a full trial of the claims on both sides, unless a settlement is reached first.

Referring to the “awful family background”, Mr Justice Richard Smith said: “The son is calling the mother a serial liar and the mother is calling the son an arch-manipulator.”

News.title: Brits say goodbye to balmy 22C weekend as temps set to plunge in parts of UK with heavy rain and thunder TODAY
News.content:
SOAK IT UP Brits say goodbye to balmy 22C weekend as temps set to plunge in parts of UK with heavy rain and thunder TODAY

AFTER a warm weekend, Brits say goodbye to the sunny weather as heavy rain and thunder are expected to hit today.

Eastern parts of the UK will be hit with cold temperatures and stormy conditions, warming up again at the end of the week.





The sun shone down on marathon runners yesterday, but this delightful dry spell is expected to break today with heavy downpours and even thunder in some areas.

While the rest of the country will escape with mostly sunny and dry conditions, clouds and cooler air over the eastern counties will keep the mercury low.

Today will start off dry for most, but cloud and rain will fall over northern Scotland before hitting the east.



Torrential rain and thunder are due to hit the Midlands, central southern England and East Anglia – all of which have experienced an unusually dry April.

In the south, warm and bright weather will continue throughout the morning but turn cloudy and drizzly this afternoon.

Heading into the evening, showers will eventually clear but leave thick clouds – especially in the east which will create misty and foggy conditions the next day.

This is down to a jet stream coming in from the east, bringing wet and windy weather.



It’s been an unusually dry April thanks to high pressure, keeping rain at bay and temperatures balmy for mid-spring.

After today’s U-turn of weather conditions, the pressure is expected to rebuild to bring more dry weather for the remaining days of the month.

On Tuesday, it will be a grey start to the day with some light showers.

The clouds should slowly lift, allowing the sun to break through and bring brighter spells.

But it will still remain cool and breezy until conditions warm up on Wednesday and Thursday.



For the rest of the month, and into May, conditions are predicted to be mostly dry and settled with temperatures hovering at or around the seasonal average.

A south-easterly wind could turn north-west Scotland very warm, with temperatures possibly reaching 20C in the Highlands by the middle of the week.



Although the weather will be mostly dry after Monday, May brings a potential threat of more rainfall if the high pressure drops again.

“On Monday, things get a little bit tricky, and down the east side of the UK, a flow comes through with the jet stream helping to bring some wet weather,” Met Office meteorologist Alex Burkill told GB News.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Different models are doing different things, but the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts model has a much wetter picture for Monday, with some heavy, perhaps thundery, rain.

“Down the eastern side of the UK, some places could see 20mm or 30mm of rain, so there is a reasonable chance that Monday will be much more unsettled than recently.”

News.title: Evil couple forced starving child to suck wall insulation for water as they tortured youngsters in vile house of horrors
News.content:
SICK & TWISTED Evil couple forced starving child to suck wall insulation for water as they tortured youngsters in vile house of horrors

A DESPICABLE couple will spend two decades behind bars after forcing one of the victims to suck wall insulation for water as part of harrowing child abuse.

Mary Hall and Jerome Norman, both 44, allegedly forced the children in their care to complete manual labour, starving them in the process.





Hall gained custody of her sister’s three children after she died in a car accident in 2018 and their father was jailed for manslaughter, WYMT reported.

Hall then moved to Pike County in Kentucky where she started a relationship with Norman.

The children’s school teachers soon started noticing worrying signs of abuse, including mysterious bruises.

To make matters worse, at least one of the children also started turning up to class with unusual patterns of hunger.



A formal complaint was made to the authorities in 2025 when one of the kids returned after an extended break extremely malnourished with a chipped tooth and damaged nose.

An investigation was immediately launched, which determined the children had been living in conditions similar to torture.

Authorities found they had been forced to live in a boarded up room that was locked from the outside.

One of the children who bore the brunt of the abuse was even forced to “suck the insulation in the walls trying to get water”, according to appointed guardian Amber Hunt.



Officials also claim the couple forced the children to do manual labour and punished them in a number of twisted ways, including withholding food.

The victims of this sickening abuse were then forced to hide the truth from their teachers and classmates.

Now, due to their fragile mental states, the children are unable to be placed in a home together.

Both Hall and Norman were sentenced to 20 years for first-degree child abuse, along with five years for each count of second-degree child abuse.

They must serve 85 per cent of their sentences – which will run concurrently – before they are eligible for parole, according to Appalachian News-Express.



The couple entered a blind Alford plea to the charges.

This means they did not admit to the crimes, but acknowledged that the evidence could likely lead to a conviction at trial.

“Our laws don’t allow for cruel and unusual punishment, even to prisoners,” Pike County Commonwealth’s Attorney Bill Slone said.

“So they’ll be subjected to the kind of punishment that they subjected those children to.”

Slone also praised school staff for speaking out, warning the outcome could have been far worse had they stayed silent.



This is not the first time a couple has stood trial for alleged child abuse.

In 2024, a Scottish couple were accused of subjecting five children in their care to a catalogue of neglect over an eleven-year period.

The pair allegedly kept the children in a “squalid” conditions at a house in Grahamston, Falkirk.

The kids, whose ages ranged from birth to 14, were allegedly in a home with dog excrement on the floors, insufficient food and drink, and a “deceased family pet” stored in the freezer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It also alleged that the property had inadequate furnishings and rubbish.



For legal reasons, none of the children can be identified.

News.title: Thousands of Gen Zs now book their holidays around their fitness goals
News.content:
SUMMER BOD Thousands of Gen Zs now book their holidays around their fitness goals

A THIRD of Gen Zs now book their holidays around their fitness goals – with one in 10 admitting access to a gym is more important to them than good weather.

Research of 2,000 adults aged 18 to 29 found 30 per cent ‘always’ or ‘often’ plan their getaways around exercise – with a total of 74 per cent having done so at one time or another.





While 47 per cent agreed fitness plans have influenced their holiday plans more than they did five years ago.

Swimming (46 per cent), walking long distances (38 per cent) and gym workouts (25 per cent) are the activities people are most likely to do to stay active while travelling, research commissioned by The Gym Group found.

Jenni Tardiff, master trainer at the nationwide, 24/7 gym, said: “It’s clear there is a shift in how younger generations combine fitness and travel.

“Holidays are no longer about rest, relaxation or over-indulgence – they’re an opportunity to stay active, set new goals and experience something different.

“Whether it’s training for an event or simply keeping up their routine by seeking out a great local gym, Gen Z are showing that fitness is a priority wherever they are in the world.”

The research also found the main reasons for seeking somewhere to work out are for mental wellbeing (33 per cent), to feel refreshed and energised (21 per cent) and to maintain routine (19 per cent).

It also emerged 44 per cent feel running a 10k or more around a new location was ‘the best way to explore it’.



And 45 per cent have prioritised suitcase space in order to fit in their running shoes, sports kit and exercise accessories.

When booking a break, 34 per cent mostly filter accommodations options to ensure they include a gym and 57 per cent are willing to pay more to have an exercise space nearby or onsite.

While 31 per cent of those who go on a staycation within the UK check to see whether they can access their local gym membership nearby more often than not.

And 42 per cent have been on a fitness-focussed trip before, centring their holiday around events such as HYROX (12 per cent), a race (16 per cent) or a retreat (20 per cent).

Of those Gen Zs who’ve been on an exercise hols, an average of £335 a year is spent on them, OnePoll.com figures found.



Many also manage to tick off other experiences whilst they’re there – including sightseeing (37 per cent), culture (29 per cent) and personal bests (27 per cent).

Jenni Tardiff, from The Gym Group, added: “What’s really interesting is that fitness-led travel isn’t about extreme training or missing out on the fun.

“For many young people, it’s about feeling good, staying grounded in familiar routines and using movement as a way to get more out of their time away.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Whether that’s a long walk, a swim or a local gym session, exercise has become a way to enhance a holiday break.”

News.title: ‘The NFL should sign him’, says unflappable Trump as he jokes about dinner gunman’s 45-yard dash before being tackled
News.content:
DONALD Trump has brushed off the shocking shooting at his black-tie dinner, joking the alleged gunman’s sprinting ability warranted an NFL contract.

The unflappable US president recalled the moment the assailant stormed his White House Correspondents dinner in an interview with 60 Minutes.





Trump said: “His speed was rather incredible actually, it was like a blur.

“He ran 45 yards and popped through, he ran like… the NFL should sign him up, he was fast.”

CCTV footage shared by Trump after the chaos unfolded showed the suspected shooter charge through security as multiple agents are knocked out of the way.

Bullets were reportedly fired with one agent being shot in the chest.

The White House said the bulletproof vest worn by the officer likely saved his life with him not suffering any major injuries.

The shooter was then quickly caught and pinned down by Secret Service agents who found he was armed with multiple weapons including a shotgun, handgun and knives.

Trump said: “When you look at it on tape it was almost like a blur.



“It was amazing because as soon as they saw that you could see they draw their guns and aim. They were so professional.”

Cole Allen, 31, was arrested on Saturday night after allegedly entering the Washington Hilton armed with two guns and knives.

Around 2,600 politicians, journalists and guests had gathered for the high-profile black-tie event.

It comes as…

President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump had taken to the stage alongside senior members of his cabinet just moments before gunfire erupted and chaos tore through the venue.



Recalling the horror moment, Trump said he was “not worried” by the third direct threat on his life in a matter of years.

He said: “I understand life. We live in a crazy world.

“My thought was, I’ve been through this before a couple of times.”

Before Saturday’s attack Allen sent loved ones a chilling manifesto, apologising for what he was about to do.

Speaking to Fox News on Sunday, Trump called the would-be assassin a “sick guy when you read his manifesto.”



“He hates Christians, that’s one thing for sure…he was a very troubled guy”, he said.

Allen now faces two counts of using a firearm during a crime of violence and assault on a federal officer with a dangerous weapon.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He is expected to be arraigned in federal court on Monday.

If convicted, he could face up to 20 years in prison for the assault charge, with the weapons offences carrying a minimum sentence of 10 years and the possibility of life imprisonment.

News.title: Klaudia Zakrzewska's mum issues heartbreaking tribute as influencer dies after Soho crash
News.content:
Klaudia Zakrzewska's mum issues heartbreaking tribute after influencer dies in Soho crash

The mum of influencer Klaudia Zakrzewska has paid tribute to the 32-year-old, describing her as a 'beautiful angel' who 'brought so much love, joy, and light into our lives'

View 3 Images Klaudia Zakrzewska's mum shared a heartbreaking tribute (Image: klaudiaglam/Instagram)

The mum of influencer Klaudia Zakrzewska has paid tribute to her "precious" daughter, who died six days after being hit by a car outside a nightclub in central London.

Klaudia, from Essex, was struck by a car on Argyll Street in Soho at 4.30am on April 19. The 32-year-old, who was known by the handle Klaudiaglam, was rushed to hospital but tragically died on Saturday.

Gabrielle Carrington - a 29-year-old former X Factor finalist - had appeared in court last Tuesday charged with attempted murder. The Metropolitan Police said on Saturday that the charge would be amended to murder following Klaudia's death.

A GoFundMe fundraiser set up last week in the name of Kinga, Klaudia's mum, described her as "in a coma and desperately fighting for her life". In an update on Monday, Kinga wrote: "My precious daughter has gained her wings and is now at peace among the angels. She brought so much love, joy, and light into our lives, and that light will never fade."

View 3 Images Klaudia Zakrzewska, a TikTok and Instagram influencer known by the handle Klaudiaglam, had over 270,000 followers on Instagram (Image: Instagram)

She continued: "As we navigate this unimaginable loss, I am committed to giving my beautiful angel the farewell she deserves, a service filled with love, dignity, and the grace that reflects who she was.

"The funds raised will go toward her funeral arrangements, ensuring she is laid to rest in the most meaningful and special way possible... Part of the donations will help cover legal fees as I pursue the best possible representation to fight for her and her memory."

Klaudia's mum also thanked people for the love and support they have shown to the family during this "incredibly difficult time". At the time of the reporting, the fundraiser has drawn in more than £26,000.

View 3 Images Gabrielle Carrington appeared in court on April 21

Article continues below

In addition to the murder charge, Carrington, of Broadfield Road, Manchester, also faces accusations of dangerous driving, drink driving, grievous bodily harm with intent and actual bodily harm. A 58-year-old man also suffered life-changing injuries following the incident, while a third woman sustained a minor wrist injury.

Carrington made it to the X Factor live finals in 2013 as one of the three members of Miss Dynamix and now has more than 365,000 followers on Instagram under the handle RIELLEUK.

She did not enter any pleas during a court hearing last week and will next appear at the Old Bailey on May 19.

News.title: DWP 'cliff edge' update on changes for Universal Credit and Housing Benefit claimants
News.content:
DWP 'cliff edge' update on changes for Universal Credit and Housing Benefit claimants

A significant change is being planned that would affect how much money claimants get to keep

View 5 Images Sir Stephen Timms has given an update on upcoming DWP changes (Image: Parliament TV)

The DWP has released an update on upcoming changes that will impact housing benefit and Universal Credit claimants who are confronted with a so-called 'cliff edge'. Ministers are putting the finishing touches to alterations in legislation that could have sweeping consequences for the financial situation of claimants.

‌



The root cause sounds complicated but is significant. Currently, claimants encounter what is known as a 'cliff edge' if they live in supported housing or temporary accommodation.

‌



This results in them facing the loss of benefits when they begin earning money. The threshold when this kicks in is now set to be revised, with adjustments expected before the year is out.

‌



View 5 Images Changes are being made that will affect housing benefit claimants (Image: sturti via Getty Images)

The rule revolves around what is termed 'earned income disregards'. The Department for Work and Pensions is seeking to increase the amount people can earn that is disregarded when calculating housing benefit.

The issue was brought into the public eye following a parliamentary question raised in recent days. Lola McEvoy, a Labour MP for Darlington, asked the DWP what the 'planned timetable is for the implementation of the earned income disregards; and what assessment he has made of the potential merits of these changes."

‌



It was announced at Rachel Reeves' Budget last year that changes would be made. But details remain to be confirmed on when it will happen.

View 5 Images The DWP has given an update on the planned changes (Image: William Barton via Getty Images)

The Budget papers said at the time: "The government is introducing new earned income disregards in Housing Benefit for claimants in supported housing and temporary accommodation. This will reduce the financial cliff edge when moving into, or progressing in, work, ensuring that work pays."

‌



Now a minister, responding to the Labour MP's question, has given more information. Stephen Timms - Minister of State (Department for Work and Pensions), said: "As announced at Autumn Budget, the department will be introducing new earned income disregards for those in receipt of Housing Benefit and live in Supported Housing and Temporary Accommodation. These disregards will help smooth the transition between the Universal Credit and Housing Benefit for individuals in Supported Housing and Temporary Accommodation as they move into work or increase their earnings, ensuring work always pays.

"The new disregards will be in place from autumn 2026. This will require legislative changes and be accompanied by IT changes made to local authority IT systems. In preparation for this, we have already begun engagement with stakeholders to ensure that the implementation meets the needs of those affected. This is accompanied by clear communications to support local authorities, housing providers and third sector organisations to ensure that eligible customers are aware of and able to utilise this change."

View 5 Images The DWP says the changes "will help smooth the transition between the Universal Credit and Housing Benefit" (Image: John_Lamb via Getty Images)

‌



Industry experts say the current system is discouraging many people from seeking employment. In a briefing note to the DWP, homelessness charity St Mungo's stated: "Supported housing exists to help people to live as independently as possible, helping improve their quality of life, their well-being, their health, and their employment prospects.

"Yet people in supported housing face a specific barrier and disincentive to work due to the way the welfare system is configured. Whereas people in receipt of benefits in the Private Rented Sector become steadily better off the more they work, people in supported housing see their benefits taken away more quickly and can actually become worse off when they work more hours.

"This is because of an anomaly in the benefit system where people in supported housing are still receiving Housing Benefit for their rent but are on Universal Credit for their living costs. The way these two benefits interact, and the high Housing Benefit taper rate (set at 65%), means that people hit a 'cliff edge' after which they become worse off as they increase their hours. This puts residents at risk of accruing arrears as the rent becomes unaffordable."

Article continues below

View 5 Images Chancellor Rachel Reeves (Image: Carl Court, Getty Images)

The charity said "because of this cliff edge and the fear of people not being able to afford their rent, we often see residents' securing jobs that they need to turn down because they are 'too many hours'." It warned that people with existing full-time jobs often ask to have hours reduced or give up work completely if part-time hours are not possible.

The noted: "Residents can also understandably be anxious about entering employment whilst in supported housing, due to the complexity and risk associated with the current benefit rules. When St Mungo's clients were asked in its 2023 survey - 'What barriers put you off from going into work, if any?' 27% of its residents stated 'I'm concerned that working whilst living in homelessness accommodation will cause problems with my benefits'."

News.title: Huge renting law change starts on Friday May 1 2026 and '£7,000 fines from June'
News.content:
Huge renting law change starts on Friday May 1 2026 and '£7,000 fines from June'

One expert has urged landlords to act 'fast' ahead of the Renters' Rights Act coming into force on Friday, May 1

View 3 Images It's a big shake-up (Image: Iryna Melnyk via Getty Images)

This Friday, the Renters' Rights Act comes into force in England, marking a landmark shake-up for the UK rental market. Ahead of the changes, one property expert has cautioned that landlords who breach the new rules could face fines running into thousands of pounds, with penalties potentially being issued as early as June.

‌



May 1, 2026 will bring a raft of significant changes to rental legislation, including the abolition of 'no-fault' (or Section 21) evictions and fixed-term contracts, with all tenancies becoming periodic, or rolling. Under the new regulations, rent increases will be restricted to once per year, and landlords could face fines of up to £40,000 for non-compliance.

‌



The long-term aim of these reforms is to establish a fairer and more stable market for tenants. In the shorter term, however, Harps Garcha, director of London-based Brooklyns Specialist Finance, has urged landlords to take one crucial step before the end of May, or risk fines of up to £7,000.

‌



She said: "If landlords haven't done anything about the upcoming changes yet - and I know there are still some that still don't quite grasp what's coming - they need to act and fast. By the end of May, as a starting point, they need to provide all named tenants individually with 'The Renters' Right Act Information Sheet 2026'.

View 3 Images The Renters’ Rights Act starts on Friday (Image: Alamy/PA)

"And please note that if there are two tenants within a specific tenancy, it needs to be provided to each individual tenant or the Local Authority could charge them up to £7,000 in fines. The sheet can be downloaded here and we suggest it's both emailed to tenants and posted to them, or, better still, hand-delivered at the property itself. And ensure you have some proof of receipt.

‌



"The sheet needs to be provided to all tenants in an Assured or Assured shorthold tenancy, and who are in a contract created before May 1, 2026, and if the tenancy has a wholly or partly written record of terms (including a written tenancy agreement)."

Harps emphasised that landlords sending the sheet via email or text must attach the actual PDF directly within the message rather than including a link to it.

She continued: "We're all used to sending links, as adding attachments can create a larger file size, especially on email, but in this case you need to send the actual document itself. Do not, under any circumstances, cut corners. Also avoid the use of WhatsApp."

Article continues below

View 3 Images Tenants will have more security (Image: Iryna Melnyk via Getty Images)

In its official documentation, the Government states clearly: "You must give this Information Sheet by May 31, 2026, or you could be fined up to £7,000."

Even for landlords who employ a lettings agent to oversee their properties and handle all administrative tasks on their behalf, Harps advised that they should "carry out this process themselves" as well. She continued: "£7,000 is a lot of money and you don't want to rely on someone else to do something when you are the one who will be liable."

News.title: Zac Efron swears by ‘12 hour rule’ that helped him 'get shredded'
News.content:
Zac Efron swears by ‘12 hour rule’ that helped him 'get shredded'

The Hollywood actor, renowned for his roles in High School Musical and The Greatest Showman, has revealed the secret behind his chiselled physique

View 4 Images Zac Efron is best known for his roles in the High School Musical films (Image: Getty Images)

Ever wondered how Zac Efron achieved his chiselled physique? Well, the Hollywood star has revealed all, including details of a lesser-known '12 hour rule' that helped him along the way.

‌



The performer, best known for his roles in The Iron Claw, High School Musical and The Greatest Showman, spoke on the Pardon My Take podcast where he divulged some of his health secrets. The first centred around the eating routine he follows to stay in shape, and it's not as simple as just cutting calories.

‌



In a conversation with hosts Dan Katz and Eric Sollenberger, who asked how Efron "got shredded", the now 38 year old explained how he avoids eating anything for 12 hours straight. This means he has his last meal of the day at around 7pm in the evening, consuming nothing other than water until the next morning.

‌



View 4 Images Zac starred in 2024's A Family Affair with Nicole Kidman (Image: Getty Images for Netflix)

Efron also explained how he incorporates longer fasting periods into his routine, adding that he will fast for a full day once a week or every two weeks. He said: "I just don't eat heavy amounts of protein just because it's healthy and all that stuff, you have 12 hours that you should not eat throughout the day.

"During your nighttime sleep cycle, say you have your dinner and your dinner ends at 7pm, you should not have anything in your body except water. A full day of fasting on one day a week or once every two weeks should follow this."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

This routine closely mirrors a form of intermittent fasting, which has gained tremendous popularity in recent years. Harvard Health Publishing claims this eating pattern cycles between periods of eating and fasting.

Research suggests intermittent fasting may help with weight management and metabolic health. A review published by National Institutes of Health found it can lead to weight loss and improvements in insulin sensitivity.

‌



View 4 Images Zac quickly became a teenage heart-throb (Image: The Daily Mirror)

However, experts warn that results can vary depending on how the fasting is implemented. According to the British Dietetic Association, some people may overeat during eating windows, which can offset any potential benefits.

Efron himself warned against overindulging during non-fasting periods. He said eating excessively in a short window, such as consuming thousands of calories in a few hours, is not advisable.

‌



The actor also highlighted the importance of balance in diet. He suggested incorporating simple, healthier meals like salads regularly, even admitting they can be an "acquired taste".

View 4 Images The cast of High School Musical, which includes Zac Efron (Image: Getty Images)

Nutrition experts say consistency is key when it comes to any diet plan. According to the NHS, maintaining a balanced diet with fruit, vegetables and whole foods is essential for long-term health.

Article continues below

Intermittent fasting is not suitable for everyone, particularly those with certain medical conditions. The NHS advises anyone considering major dietary changes to seek professional guidance first.

While Efron’s routine may work for him, experts stress that there is no one-size-fits-all approach. Sustainable habits and balanced nutrition remain the most widely recommended way to stay healthy.

News.title: Women writers dominate in new Booktok bestseller list announced by TikTok
News.content:
Women writers dominate in new Booktok bestseller list announced by TikTok

TikTok launches the UK's first official #BookTok Bestseller List for the National Year of Reading 2026. Female authors dominate the inaugural top 20 as the app fuels a £86million publishing boom.

View 3 Images Three books are sold every minute on TikTok shop (Image: Getty Images)

TikTok has officially formalised its massive influence on the British publishing industry by launching the UK’s first #BookTok Bestseller List.

‌



Created in partnership with data specialists Media Control and NielsenIQ BookData, the new monthly chart combines verified physical retail sales with in-app engagement metrics to provide a definitive look at the titles truly resonating with young readers today.

‌



The launch comes as part of a wider collaboration with the Department for Education and the National Literacy Trust for the National Year of Reading 2026. This government-backed initiative aims to reverse a decline in reading for pleasure, with TikTok now serving as a primary discovery tool for over half of all 16 to 25-year-olds in the UK.

‌



View 3 Images The Booktok bestseller list is part of a collaboration for the National Year of Reading (Image: TikTok)

5 must-read books that made top authors fall in love with reading READ MORE :

Women's Prize for Fiction 2026 shortlist spotlights fresh voices and small publishers READ MORE :

Recent figures suggest the #BookTok community has become an economic powerhouse, driving more than 11 million book sales and generating approximately £86 million for the UK publishing industry in the last year alone.

The inaugural top 20, which will be updated on a monthly basis, is comprised entirely of female authors. Irish writer Chloe Walsh emerged as the standout name, with all six books in her Boys of Tommen series - which follows a group of teenagers navigating love, friendship, and trauma at a private school.

‌



The rankings also highlight the dominance of "romantasy," the platform’s most popular genre, with high-profile titles from Sarah J. Maas and Rebecca Yarros featuring prominently.

Beyond current trends, the chart reflects how #BookTok is fundamentally reshaping the lifecycle of books by breathing new life into older titles. A notable example is Donna Tartt’s The Secret History. Despite being first published in 1992, it has secured a spot on the list after finding a fresh audience decades later through viral digital recommendations.

View 3 Images The Booktok bestseller list sees women writers take all the top spots (Image: TikTok)

‌



By merging social media trends with actual till sales, the list identifies viral sensations that traditional charts may overlook. To bridge the gap between digital discovery and the high street, books featured on the monthly list will now be eligible for official #BookTok Bestseller stickers in physical bookstores.

Major publishers including Penguin Random House and HarperCollins have already embraced the system as a way to connect their authors with the app's hyper-engaged audience.

Dominic Burns, Head of Operations at TikTok UK, noted that what began as a niche community conversation has evolved into a global movement that is bringing a new generation back into local bookshops. Burns comments: "Since TikTok’s inception, #BookTok has grown into a vibrant global community that has not only shaped the literary conversation but has fuelled bestsellers and brought a new generation ba ck into local bookshops.

‌



"To celebrate this milestone year, we’re inviting everyone to join the World’s Biggest Book Club on TikTok, bringing readers together through unique online and in-person moments, to share the stories they love."

Want to hear the latest books news and reviews from The Mirror's resident bookworm? Follow Aimée Walsh on Tiktok and Instagram

‌



David Hayman, Director of the National Year of Reading 2026, welcomed the partnership, stating that platforms like TikTok play a vital role in making reading feel relevant and accessible to young people through shared passion and creativity. Hayman said: "The National Year of Reading 2026 is about supporting people across the UK to rediscover the joy and power of reading in ways that feel relevant to them.

"Communities like #BookTok are playin g a vital role in this, inspiring a new generation of readers through creativity, connection and shared passion. We're delighted to partner with TikTok to celebrate the World’s Biggest Book Club and encourage everyone to 'Go All In' on their passions and interests through reading."

The bestseller list serves as the foundation for the "World’s Biggest Book Club," a programme of events scheduled throughout 2026. This includes a return to the Hay Festival as an official digital media partner and the debut of #BookTok LIVE, a multi-sensory event designed to bring the online community together in person.

Article continues below

With three books currently selling every minute on TikTok Shop in the UK, the platform is now positioning itself as a central pillar of the nation's literary culture.

Love reading? Join Dr. Aimée Walsh and our community of fellow readers in the Mirror Book Club to dive deeper into the books everyone is talking about.

News.title: Lidl offering everyone potentially big money reward to spot new supermarket store sites
News.content:
Lidl offers £1,000s to anyone who can find locations for its new stores

Budget supermarket Lidl has published a list of more than 1,000 towns and cities across the UK where it might open new stores - along with a reward for anyone who helps it

View 3 Images Discount supermarket has listed more than 1,000 places for potential store openings (Image: In Pictures via Getty Images)

Budget supermarket Lidl is offering members of the public a chunk of money to find spots for new stores.

‌



The grocer has published a list of more than 1,000 places across the UK where it could potentially open branches. They stretch from Inverness and Ellon in Scotland, to St Ives in Cornwall and Ryde on the Isle of Wight, as well as in Wales and Northern Ireland.

‌



Despite having its owns property teams, as well as agents around the country, Lidl says it wants shoppers’ help too.

‌



As an added perks, the retailer is offering a finder’s fee to anyone who successfully identifies a previously unknown site that leads to a developed store. The amount is worth 1.5% of how much the store’s freehold was bought for, or 10% of the first year’s rent on a leasehold.

View 3 Images Lidl opened its 1,000th UK store last November (Image: PaulMaguire via Getty Images)

Reports from 2022 said the finder’s fee available at the time could have been worth £22,500 on finding a £1.5million freehold site that Lidl bought outright.

‌



Lidl was asked whether any members of the public have actually bagged that sort of bumper sum, given there are property agents whose job it is to find such sites. A spokeswoman claimed: "We wouldn’t be able to provide specifics on individuals or partners involved in site introductions as those arrangements are commercially sensitive."

And while the German-owned chain Lidl may have the more than 1,000 sites in mind for new stores, as well as relocating existing branches from nearby, it is unlikely to be opening most any time soon.

View 3 Images St Ives in Cornwall is just one of the more than 1,000 places across the UK Lidl says might open new stores (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



Lidl to launch brand new budget mobile phone plans - but only for certain shoppers READ MORE :

Lidl, part of the Schwarz retail group, has more than 1,000 UK stores already - it reached the milestone with a store in East Grinstead last November - and is adding more than 50 over the next 12 months as part of a £600m expansion.

Lidl’s brochure for new sites includes 65 in Scotland; 49 in North East England; 71 in Yorkshire and Humber; 62 in Greater Manchester and the surrounding area; 52 in North Wales, Merseyside, and the west of Cheshire; 72 in Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire, Shropshire, Staffordshire and east Cheshire; 47 in south and mid Wales; 80 in central England; 69 in eastern England; 43 in Bristol, Gloucestershire, Wiltshire, and parts of Somerset; 69 in the Home Counties north of London; 139 in north London; 102 in south London; 42 in south and west Somerset, Devon and Cornwall; 56 towards the south coast of England; and 61 in Kent, East Sussex and East Surrey.

Richard Taylor, chief real estate officer at Lidl GB, said: “We currently have one of the most ambitious store opening programmes of any supermarket and we are more committed than ever to bringing our high quality and low priced products to even more communities across the country.

Article continues below

“All of our stores deliver more than just affordable products. Each one also brings quality jobs, opportunities for British suppliers to showcase the best of our home grown produce and support to local good causes in the communities each one serves. In uncertain times, shoppers and communities can count on us.”

News.title: Deadly strike at Europe's biggest nuclear power plant as chilling warning issued
News.content:
Deadly strike at Europe's biggest nuclear power plant as chilling warning issued

An employee has been killed in a drone attack on the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant carried out by Ukrainian Armed Forces, Russia's State Atomic Energy Corporation has said

View 2 Images A worker has been killed in a strike at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Russia says (file photo) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has issued an urgent warning after a deadly attack at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine.

‌



Russia's State Atomic Energy Corporation said a driver was killed by a drone strike in an operation carried out by Ukrainian Armed Forces.

‌



The Rosatom corporation said an employee at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant had been killed in the strike this morning.

‌



The Russian agency said the strike was a “great tragedy” and added that attacks on the nuclear plant “pose a threat not only to people but also to security as a whole”.

Meanwhile the IAEA's Director General said in a statement today that strikes on or near nuclear power plants (NPPs) can endanger nuclear safety and "must not take place".

View 2 Images Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Station was seized by forces in 2022 (Image: AP)

‌



The IAEA statement said: "IAEA has been informed by the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant that a drone strike this morning killed a driver at its transport workshop in the vicinity of the plant site.

"Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi reiterates that strikes on or near NPPs can endanger nuclear safety and must not take place. The IAEA’s team on the site will look into the incident and continue to monitor the situation."

In a separate statement Russian agency Rosatom, which has controlled the plant since it was captured by Russian forces, said: "A Zaporizhzhia NPP employee has been killed in a strike by the Ukrainian Armed Forces

‌



"Today, a driver was killed as a result of a strike by a Ukrainian Armed Forces drone on the premises of the transport workshop at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant."

The plant bosses called the man's death "a terrible and irreplaceable loss," adding that "employees of the nuclear industry must not be targeted." They continued: "Any attacks on the Zaporizhzhia NPP pose a threat not only to people but also to security as a whole. It is a blow to life and to the future."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



On March 4 2022 Russian troops seized Zaporizhzhia NPP, the largest nuclear power plant in Europe.

In a speech yesterday to mark the the 40th anniversary of the nuclear disaster at the Chernobyl plant in Ukraine, the country's Ambassador to the UN Andrii Melnyk called for Russian forces to "finally get the hell out of the occupiedZaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant".

Mr Melnyk said the Zaporizhzhia plant "remains under occupation to this very day as a hostage, terrorizing not only Ukraine but the entire international community."

Article continues below

Calling for sanctions against Russia's nuclear energy industry he added: "This nuclear blackmail, this nuclear nightmare must end. Russia has to return the plant to Ukraine immediately and unconditionally and ensure its safety in accordance with IAEA standards."

News.content:
Plane bursts into flames during take-off as passengers evacuated on slides and injured

Six passengers suffered injuries after the engine of a Swiss International Air Lines plane burst into flames during take-off at Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi, India

Passengers evacuated from plane on runway after engine fire in New Delhi

Six plane passengers were injured while being evacuated via emergency slides after an engine caught on fire during take-off.

‌



Footage filmed from inside the cabin shows firefighters hosing down the affected engine at Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi, India, in the early hours yesterday.

‌



Other clips show passengers sliding down onto the tarmac. According to local reports, one of the 15-year-old Airbus A330-343’s two engines caught fire seconds into the take-off run.

‌



Swiss International Air Lines said in a statement: “There were 228 passengers and four infants on board. Shortly after takeoff, just after 1am local time in India, an issue occurred with one of the engines.

View 3 Images Six passengers were injured after the incident (Image: JamPress)

“The crew rejected the takeoff and, following an assessment of the situation, decided as a precaution to evacuate the aircraft. Six passengers currently receiving medical attention, crew unharmed.”

‌



The injuries are believed to have been minor and sustained during the evacuation. Swiss said the affected passengers were being rebooked onto other flights or accommodated in hotels.

The airline added: “We are determined to fully understand what led to this incident. Swiss technical specialists will travel to Delhi to inspect the aircraft and initiate the next steps.

View 3 Images Fire engines met the plane (Image: JamPress)

‌



“At the same time, we are working intensively to find swift and suitable onward travel solutions for all passengers. The safety of our passengers and our crew is always our top priority.”

This comes after the boss of a major airline warned more flight cancellations are coming after his firm was forced to axe some journeys from the UK.

Norse Atlantic Airways CEO Eivind Roald has already cancelled flights from London Gatwick Airport to Los Angeles. He says he had to act after the price of jet fuel skyrocketed “more than 100 per cent after a few days”.

News.title: Sawe smashes two-hour mark to 'move goalposts for marathon running'
News.content:
Sabastian Sawe made history at the London Marathon by becoming the first athlete to run a sub-two-hour marathon in a competitive race.

The 31-year-old Kenyan crossed the line to win in one hour 59 minutes 30 seconds, more than one minute faster than the late Kelvin Kiptum's previous record of 2:00:35, set in 2023.

The great Eliud Kipchoge became the first man to run a marathon in under two hours in 2019, but that was not record-eligible as it was held under controlled conditions.

Already on world record pace as he crossed the halfway mark in 1:00:29, Sawe was able to speed up over the second half of the race to run even faster than Kipchoge's time.

Sawe made his decisive move before the final 10km, with only debutant Yomif Kejelcha able to cover his surge off the front.

Remarkably, Kejelcha, making his marathon debut, became the second man to run under two hours in race conditions, finishing runner-up in 1:59:41.

Half marathon world record holder Jacob Kiplimo also crossed the line faster than Kiptum's former record, completing the podium in 2:00:28.

Sawe, speaking on BBC TV, said: "I am feeling good. I am so happy. It is a day to remember for me."

"We started the race well. Approaching finishing the race, I was feeling strong. Finally reaching the finish line, I saw the time, and I was so excited."

The Belgian coastal town of De Panne recently became the unlikely stage for the annual European seagull screeching championship, where more than 70 contestants gathered to perfect their imitation of the bird's distinctive shriek. On Sunday, participants from 15 countries converged for the sixth edition of this unique competition.

Held within the lively confines of a local pub, the event attracted a diverse array of attendees, from families with young children to seasoned competitors, many of whom embraced the spirit by sporting seagull-themed costumes. Each attempt at mimicking the seabird's call was met with enthusiastic cheers from the appreciative crowd.

A panel of judges meticulously scored each performance, allocating up to 15 points for the fidelity of the seagull sound and an additional five points for the competitor's stage presence. This quirky tradition, now firmly established, seeks to transform the public image of seagulls, which are often perceived as bothersome.

Claude Willaert, the event’s organiser, underscored this positive message. "When you are on holiday, you always remember the waves of the sea and the calls of the seagulls," he remarked. "So be positive about them."

Competitors take part in the sixth edition of the European seagull screeching championship, in which contestants compete either solo or as part of a group and are judged by a jury for vocal skills and performance ( Reuters )

In 2024, a young British boy named Cooper won the contest after proving he could screech better than even some seagulls.

Cooper, from Chesterfield, Derbyshire, discovered his talent after being bitten by a seagull who had taken a fancy to the tuna sandwich he was eating.

A big Spiderman fan, Cooper concluded this would enable him to become “Seagull Boy” in the way that Peter Parker became a spindly superhero after a spider bite.

However, his mum admitted that his squawk has taken some getting used to, but the family were ultimately happy to support Cooper because of his undeniable talent.

“People would start to turn around and look for the seagull,” she said.

Twinkle-toed Michael Jackson fans are using screenings of the singer’s new biopic to show off their dancing skills – and the results are dividing cinemagoers, with some saying “don’t stop ‘til you get enough” and others urging them to “beat it”.

Despite a mauling from critics, Michael is proving to be a box office hit, setting a new record for music biopics in its opening weekend.

Many of these showings are turning into dance parties, with fans performing Jackson’s routines at the same time as lead star Jaafar Jackson, the singer’s very own nephew, in front of the screen.

This has prompted widespread debate, with the majority of viewers accusing the “annoying” moonwalking individuals of ruining their filmgoing experience. They’ve accused the people of having “main character syndrome”, complaining that they have paid to watch a film, not attend a concert.

open image in gallery Michael Jackson’s nephew Jaafar plays singer in hit biopic ( Universal Pictures )

“There’s a difference between enjoying the moment and disrupting everyone else’s experience,” one viewer wrote on social media. “Not everyone paid to watch a live performance.”

Another told the excitable fans to “save the moonwalk for outside”, with many linking it to a rise in poor audience etiquette in which people use their phones and talk loudly while watching the film. “It’s part of the reason I’m avoiding screenings right now,” one person stated on X/Twitter.

Many said they would ask for refunds if they were in attendance when a similar thing happened.

However, some have praised the electric, convivial atmosphere caused by the dancing fans who “took over” the cinema, comparing it to repertory screenings of 1975 cult musical The Rocky Horror Picture Show.

“People were dancing at the front of the screen like it was a live concert. This wasn’t a movie… this was a full-blown MJ revival,” one viewer said, with another calling it “one of the best moviegoing experiences I've had in my life”.

open image in gallery 'Michael' screenings are becoming dance parties – much to the annoyance of cinemagoers ( Universal Pictures )

“The audience was fully locked in from start to finish (dancing/fully enjoying themselves). It was magical,” they wrote.

A similar debate raged last year following the release of The Minecraft Movie. One moment in the film saw Jack Black and Jason Momoa’s characters confronted in a boxing ring by a cuboid Minecraft chicken, who is ridden around the ring by another character.

“Chicken jockey!” exclaims Black’s character, a reference to the video game that seems to be sending audiences wild.

Footage captured across social media showed food and popcorn being thrown across the audience when this moment occurred, along with loud shouting, swearing and people jumping out of their seats. Young people could be seen laughing with their phones out as they captured the disorder, which became a popular TikTok trend.

Special screenings encouraging the raucous behaviour were ultimately organised in order to lure people away from screenings filled with people who wanted to watch the film in peace.

The heady scent of tea tree is one of the iconic smells of the Australian bush. And the essential oils derived from tea trees have been used as medicines, first by Indigenous people, then by colonists.

Today, many of us have a bottle of tea tree oil at home, or use shampoo or creams containing it. Tea tree oil is also a major export earner for Australia.

Now, media reports suggest the European Union (EU) is concerned that tea tree oil may affect people’s fertility and may ban imports.

Let’s see whether we really need to worry about any impact of tea tree oil on our reproductive system.

The many uses of tea tree oil

Leaves of Melaleuca alternifolia trees and other species of Melaleuca produce an essential oil that’s used medicinally and in a variety of toiletries and cosmetics. This oil is a complex mixture of nearly 100 aromatic compounds.

Tea tree oil has been used as an antiseptic since it became commercially available in the 1930s. It has antibacterial, antifungal, anti-parasite and antioxidant properties.

Tea tree oil has been used as an antiseptic since it became commercially available in the 1930s ( Getty )

Laboratory experiments suggest it may also help reduce inflammation and enhance healing.

It’s used to treat acne, seborrhoeic dermatitis, and as a mouthwash to treat gingivitis (gum disease). However, the clinical evidence for these uses is not strong.

Tea tree oil is also used in cosmetics and toiletries, such as shower gel and face wash, in various concentrations.

Is tea tree oil safe?

The most common adverse effects of tea tree oil are when it’s used on the skin. In some people, the skin can become sensitive and allergic contact dermatitis can develop. This is particularly when used neat (using the pure oil) rather than after using cosmetics and toiletries, which contain lower concentrations.

Acute toxicity, when there are rapid side-effects coming on within minutes, to tea tree oil via skin application is rare.

Drinking tea tree oil, even diluted or in small concentrations, is not recommended as this can be deadly. There have been reports of cases of depression of the central nervous system (where brain activity slows down) and possible injury to the lungs.

How about the reproductive system?

The EU has been concerned about the potential impact of tea tree oil on the reproductive system for several years.

In November 2023, the European Chemicals Agency’s Committee for Risk Assessment proposed that tea tree oil be classified as a presumed human reproductive toxicant, under category IB.

This classification would mean a ban on tea tree oil in pesticides, and cosmetics and toiletries used in the EU.

The decision rested on the results of reproductive toxicity experiments. This involved administering tea tree oil to rats orally at various concentrations for ten days, before mating. Female rats also received tea tree oil while pregnant and up to the weaning of the offspring.

About the author Ian Musgrave is a Senior Lecturer in Pharmacology at Adelaide University. This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

In the females, measures of fertility, including the number of embryos implanted and mean litter size, were no different to those that had not been given tea tree oil.

At the highest doses, the sperm counts of male rats were lower. But this wasn’t the case for rats given tea tree at 25 milligrams of tea tree oil per kilogram of body-weight per day. That’s around 0.028 millilitres of tea tree oil per kilogram a day.

This doesn’t sound much, but for a 60kg human, that would be equivalent to drinking about one-and-a-half millilitres of pure tea tree oil a day. Nobody is going to be drinking that amount day in, day out. Virtually every application says not to ingest any tea tree oil because of its known human oral toxicity.

This is the level that has no effect on reproduction. The level for reproductive toxicity is twice that.

In cosmetics and toiletries, no-one would be exposed to that much tea tree oil. Less than 4% of tea tree oil components are absorbed via the skin. So even if you did smear that much tea tree oil on yourself, the concentration your body would be exposed to is less than a tenth of the amount that has no effect.

Rats also metabolise tea tree oil components differently to humans. They produce a toxic byproduct that affects sperm. By comparison, humans only produce trace levels of this byproduct.

So what happened recently?

In November 2025, another European committee, the Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety gave its update.

It considered the issues of dose and metabolism outlined above. It also considered human pharmacovigilance data (where therapies are monitored over time to track any potential safety issues). The pharmacovigilance data showed no sign of reproductive toxicity associated with human use of existing products.

It considered tea tree oil’s use in cosmetics and toiletries to be safe up to the maximum concentration of:

2.0% in shampoo

1.0% in shower gel

1.0% in face wash

0.1% in face cream.

The United Kingdom has also weighed in. In August 2025, the Health and Safety Executive didn’t classify tea tree oil as a reproductive toxicant.

What this means for the EU’s classification of tea tree oil in the future is unclear. Shifting it to another category – toxicity category 2, a suspected human reproductive toxicant – would be an option.

In a nutshell

Europe’s initial evaluation of tea tree oil as a presumed human reproductive toxicant in 2023 understandably sounds alarming. But the 2025 update has toned down warnings.

The subsequent re-evaluation of evidence – of tea tree oil’s concentrations and applications, species-specific toxicity, and real-world data tracking safety in humans – means we can be much more confident of its safety.

Tea tree oil, when used as directed, is much safer than the headlines suggest.

News.title: Trump admits he ‘wasn’t making it easy’ for Secret Service during WHCD shooting
News.content:
Donald Trump said he “didn’t make it any easier” for Secret Service agents as they rushed him to safety when gunshots were fired during the White House Correspondents’ Dinner on Saturday (25 April).

Speaking to CBS correspondent Norah O’Donnell on 60 Minutes after the shooting, the US president said: “I wanted to see what was happening, and I wasn't making it that easy for him. I wanted to see what was going on... I probably made them act a little bit more slowly.”

A suspected gunman attempted to storm the annual dinner at the Washington Hilton hotel at 8:30 p.m., with shots fired before he was apprehended by the Secret Service.

The suspected shooter has been identified as 31-year-old California man Cole Tomas Allen. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has said that investigators believe Allen was targeting members of the Trump administration.

News.title: Ronnie O’Sullivan v John Higgins LIVE: Old rivals battle for quarter-final place at World Snooker Championship
News.content:
Ronnie O'Sullivan (right) and John Higgins battle for a quarter-final place ( PA )

The latest clash between old rivals Ronnie O’Sullivan and John Higgins is bubbling away nicely as they battle for a quarter-final place at the World Snooker Championship.

“The Rocket” looked to be closing in on the last eight when he powered into a 9-4 lead on Sunday evening, only for Higgins to peg him back as the Scot won the final three frames of the session to leave the match intriguingly poised. O’Sullivan, who had scored freely to open up that advantage, thumped the table in frustration after missing a red in the 16th frame, and must re-find his touch if he is to advance.

Two members of the “Class of ‘92”, the pair have 11 world titles between them with O’Sullivan hoping to move clear of Stephen Hendry by securing an eighth Crucible crown. Can his familiar foe derail that tilt at history? The match resumes just after 1pm BST.

Follow all of the latest from the Crucible in Sheffield with our live blog below:

A government minister could not confirm if the King would take part in a walkabout on his state visit to the US after adjustments were made to his security arrangements following an attempted shooting in Washington.

King Charles’ security was reviewed following an attempted attack on Donald Trump at a dinner on Saturday night, with the Palace confirming on Sunday that the visit would proceed.

Asked about whether he would take part in a walkabout on the trip - an informal public walk taken by members of the Royal Family to greet members of the public - environment minister Emma Reynolds told Times Radio: "I can't comment specifically on the security provisions. But what I will say is that every measure is taken to protect the King and the Queen.

“And they will obviously have looked very carefully at the events of the weekend, which were very, very concerning.

King Charles with US President Donald Trump at Windsor Castle during the president’s 2025 state visit to the UK (PA) ( PA Archive )

“But every measure will be taken. The King's security is something that is planned and they schedule weeks and months in advance. But obviously, they will be looking at what happened over the weekend."

Charles and Camilla’s security arrangements were discussed in the wake of Saturday’s violent incident at a Washington media dinner where Mr Trump, the first lady and senior figures from his administration were bundled from the room by the secret service after shots were fired.

Following questions over whether or not the visit would go ahead, Buckingham Palace confirmed on Sunday night that it would proceed after “discussions on both sides of the Atlantic through the day”.

“The King and Queen are most grateful to all those who have worked at pace to ensure this remains the case and are looking forward to the visit getting underway tomorrow [Monday]”, the palace added.

It is understood there will be some modest operational adjustments to one or two royal engagements during the trip but the overall plan remains as previously outlined.

The White House Correspondents’ Association dinner was thrown into chaos on Saturday night after the attempted attack, which saw shots fired, prompting the US President to be swiftly evacuated by Secret Service agents along with other senior members of his administration.

Speaking to Fox News on Sunday about the King’s state visit, Mr Trump said: “He’s coming and we’re going to have a great time.”

He added: “He’s a great guy, and we look forward to it. He’s really a fantastic person and a tremendous representative, and he’s brave.

“We’re gonna have a great time. And he represents his nation like nobody else can do it.”

The suspect, said to have been carrying a shotgun and handgun, has been identified as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California.

He is understood to have been a guest in the Washington Hilton hotel, where the event was being held. He faces charges including assaulting an officer with a dangerous weapon, but acting attorney general Todd Blanche said additional charges will be filed.

The president posted pictures on his Truth Social platform of the alleged assailant handcuffed on the ground following his detention, and described him as a “lone wolf whack job”.

Mr Trump – who was attending the annual dinner for the first time as president – vowed to reschedule the disrupted event at a late-night press conference following the shooting, which he said had “unified” political opponents and the media.

It is understood that the King and Queen reached out privately to the US president and first lady over the weekend to express their sympathies with all those affected by the shooting and their gratitude to the security services who prevented further injury.

The historic visit, the King’s first visit to the US as monarch, will mark the 250th anniversary of American independence and herald the start of celebrations across the US.

The royal couple, who will begin their visit with a private tea hosted by the president and first lady, are also expected to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks that brought down New York’s Twin Towers.

Later, Mr Trump and the King are expected sit down for talks in the White House’s famous Oval Office while Camilla and Melania Trump take part in an event together.

Sir Keir Starmer will chair another Cobra meeting this week to discuss the ongoing economic impact of the Iran war, which he warned could continue “for some time”.

The prime minister will convene the emergency committee with representatives from the Bank of England to discuss the war’s economic consequences in the shadow of rising oil prices.

The meeting comes as oil prices hit a near three-week high on Monday, as the Strait of Hormuz remains blockaded as peace talks between the US and Iran stall.

Speaking in Lancashire on Monday, the prime minister said he had called the meeting on Tuesday “so you can be sure we will stand by working people in this crisis”.

However, he told the Usdaw union’s conference: “I have to level with you about Iran.

“The truth is the economic consequences could still be with us for some time.

The prime minister said he had called the meeting on Tuesday ‘so you can be sure we will stand by working people in this crisis’ ( Reuters )

“You don’t need to be a politician to know that, you can see it on every petrol forecourt across the country.”

On Sunday, the chief secretary to the prime minister, Darren Jones, warned price hikes as a result of the conflict will be felt for at least eight months after the war ends.

He said people will see higher energy, food and flight prices “as a consequence of what Donald Trump has done in the Middle East” and said there will be a “long tail from this”.

This is a breaking news story, more to follow...
