Sports.title: Sir Chris Hoy shares cancer update after being told he had four years to live in 2023
Sports.content:
Sir Chris Hoy shares cancer update after being told he had four years to live in 2023

Legendary British Olympian Sir Chris Hoy has shared an update about his health nearly three years after he was diagnosed with stage 4 cancer

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy is battling terminal cancer (Image: BBC)

Sir Chris Hoy has provided an update on his health nearly three years after he was diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer.

‌



The 50-year-old six-time gold medal winning Olympian originally said he was told that he had four years to live when he announced his tragic diagnosis in September 2023. Should the prediction be accurate, it would mean the cyclist tragically has less than 18 months left to live.

‌



However, in his latest update, one of Britain’s most successful Olympians has said he was trying to “hang in there” as long as he could until new medicines arrived that could prolong his life.

‌



Sir Chris hopes that AI could be used to help develop new medicines. He explained: “It’s going relatively well and I’m just kind of cracking on with life…. You’ve got to find a way to enjoy the moment and enjoy the day but also put faith in the people that are doing all these incredible things.

“There could be an amazing treatment just around the corner if you can hang in there. There are a lot of issues with AI in the future and we have got to manage it well, but one of the real positives of AI has to be in the field of medicine and the rate at which we can develop and optimise new drugs for treatment in the future.”

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy (Image: Sam Mellish, Getty Images)

‌



Sir Chris also talked on his podcast Sporting Misadventures about how he was encouraged by the progress of immunotherapy treatments being developed, praising it for the fact that it can target just the cancer and not attack the surrounding tissues.

However, he admitted it had not been possible for him to have immunotherapy due to the type of cancer he has.

He continued: “There is a new trial drug which may well have cracked it and it should be available relatively soon. By all accounts it’s having remarkable success in terms of the number of patients in the trial who responded well to it.”

‌



View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy has shared a health update (Image: Angel Martinez, Getty Images for Laureus)

Sir Chris’ update comes just a few months after he launched a campaign to raise awareness of the condition, launching a screening campaign with rugby player Kenny Logan earlier this year.

The point of the campaign was to encourage men to sign up and get scanned so that potential cases of the cancer could be spotted earlier. In response, around 6,000 men signed up to the Scottish Prostate Cancer Initiative within seven days.

Article continues below

Speaking at the time about the impact of prostate cancer on him, Sir Chris said: “A stage four diagnosis changes your life drastically but I guess it's finding a new purpose, and today's event is all about trying to educate men about the importance of catching prostate cancer early. Early detection saves lives – that is the message to take away from today.”

Sports.title: Boxing title fight chaos as fans storm ring and CHAIRS thrown in violent mass brawl
Sports.content:
Boxing title fight chaos as fans storm ring and CHAIRS thrown in violent mass brawl

Emirhan Kalkan's UBO title fight with Sergei Gorokhov took a sinister turn when fans burst into the ring, sparking a mass brawl in which chairs and unsanctioned punches were sent flying

View 2 Images A brawl erupted during a boxing title fight (Image: X)

A professional world championship boxing bout took an unruly turn when a violent mass brawl erupted inside the ring. Turkey's Emirkhan Kalkhan and Russia's Sergei Gorokhov met at the Besirli Sports Hall in a showdown for the UBO world championship.

‌



However, tensions boiled over after the second round, after Gorokhov secured a stoppage win over his opponent on the night. The boxer was elated as he celebrated with his cornermen before walking over to Kalkhan to seemingly check in on his opponent.

‌



A member of Kalkhan's team then pushed Gorokhov back, before one of his cornermen rushed over to give a push of his own. Matters got out of hand as the two respective team-mates began to brawl, before fans surrounding stormed into the squared-circle to trade punches and kicks of their own.

‌



Plastic chairs were thrown into the ring, as Gorokhov's trainer was beaten and kicked by a group of men. The boxer was also blindsided as he pleaded with them to stop, before he was pounced upon by another group.

As he hit the ground, Gorokhov was beaten with chairs and kicked at, as he disappeared under a wave of melee. A separate video, meanwhile, shows Gorokhov's cornerman, Igor Sudalainen, lying on the floor holding his head as security and some members of Kalkhan's team attempted to intervene.

View 2 Images Sergei Gorokhov and his team were attacked (Image: X)

‌



In the aftermath, Gorokhov took to social media to share an update from a local hospital. Taking to the stories section of his Instagram account, he said: "Hello everyone. We’re currently in a hospital in Turkey.

"Ismail [trainer] has suffered a head injury and is having an MRI scan right now. I’ve come through it the least badly. The gloves helped protect me. Who saw the broadcast? There were probably about 80 people there attacking us.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"They got in the ring and beat us up after our brilliant victory in the second round, where we knocked this fighter out twice. But the Turks behaved very badly.

"But thank God, everyone is alive. That’s the sort of brawl that happened, a tough one. I’ll tell you more later. We’ve got a police escort now; we’ll head straight from the hotel to our rooms.

"I don’t think we’ll be staying there tonight. If anyone tries to pull a stunt, we’ll fly straight to Georgia. Then we’ll drive through Georgia overnight to Mineralnye Vody, and from there to Kaliningrad.

Article continues below

"Thanks to everyone for your support. We’ll be in touch. I’ll tell you everything tomorrow. The world champion’s belt – we’ve got a world champion in Russia, in Kaliningrad, in boxing. It was a very good fight."

Gorokhov later shared another video on Instagram, confirming that he and his team had safely arrived in Georgia. He said: "We are in Georgia. We have the belt, we are the champions. Thank you very much for your support friends."

Sports.title: Tottenham face rearranged fixture where relegation could be confirmed at arch rivals
Sports.content:
Tottenham face rearranged fixture where relegation could be confirmed at arch rivals

Tottenham will see their clash with Chelsea rearranged due to the Blues making the FA Cup final - leaving them with the prospect of being relegated at Stamford Bridge if results go against them

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi still faces a huge fight to keep Tottenham in the Premier League

Tottenham's penultimate Premier League game of the season against Chelsea will need to be rearranged after the Blues made the FA Cup final - and could leave the north Londoners in a do-or-die situation.

‌



The two sides had been due to meet at Stamford Bridge on Sunday May 17, but the FA Cup final is the day prior and the west London side will face Manchester City at Wembley. It leaves them and Tottenham needing to find a new date before the final day of the season on Sunday May 24.

‌



A date for the rearranged fixture between Tottenham and Chelsea is expected to be announced imminently, but it is likely to take place after the FA Cup final. Tottenham themselves are playing a home to Leeds on Monday May 11, which makes it almost impossible for the game to be played in that midweek.

‌



If it is rearranged for the days leading up to the final day, where Tottenham face Everton at home, then they will play after relegation rivals West Ham have taken on Newcastle at St James’ Park.

It means a situation exists whereby Tottenham, who are already two points off the Hammers, may need to respond to West Ham's result and anything but a win at Chelsea could relegate them.

Xavi Simons stretchered off as Tottenham suffer another huge injury blow vs Wolves READ MORE :

Tottenham relegation fears grow despite win as West Ham bag huge result in drop battle READ MORE :

It adds further spice to a fixture that has previously seen tensions boil over. It was in 2016 that a draw with the Blues saw Tottenham miss out on the title and crown Leicester. They had led 2-0 that night before conceding twice as tempers flared with Tottenham receiving a record nine yellow cards.

‌



Tottenham only have four games to save their season and head to Aston Villa this weekend before hosting Leeds. Saturday saw them win a first league game in 2026 as they narrowly saw off already relegated Wolves, Joao Palhinha scoring a second-half winner.

View 2 Images Joao Palhinha's goal helped Tottenham see off Wolves

The blow for Tottenham was a stoppage time strike for West Ham, which saw them pick up three points at home to Everton. It leaves Roberto De Zerbi's side on 34 points, two shy of the Hammers. A thumping win for Nottingham Forest on Friday means they are five points clear of the north Londoners.

Article continues below

De Zerbi said after their win at Molineux: "I'm happy for the result. I hope this result can change something in our head, in our mentality for the other results. It's already very tough to win a game for us. If we put our heads on the other teams, it becomes too tough for me."

Sports.title: Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri sent blunt warning by Marseille boss after yet another snub
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri sent blunt warning by Marseille boss after yet another snub

Ethan Nwaneri was left on the bench by manager Habib Beye as Marseille were held to a 1-1 draw by Nice on Sunday, with the Arsenal loanee's frustrating situation continuing

View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri's time at Marseille hasn't been straightforward (Image: Franco Arland/Getty Images)

Ethan Nwaneri has been warned about his "day-to-day commitment" after being left on the bench by Marseille manager Habib Beye. The Arsenal loanee didn't make it onto the pitch as Marseille were held to a 1-1 draw by Nice in Ligue 1 on Sunday.

‌



Nwaneri moved to the south of France in January in search of regular first-team football, having struggled for minutes at title-chasing Arsenal. But the move hasn't worked out how he'd hoped, with Roberto De Zerbi leaving to be replaced by Beye.

‌



The 19-year-old is yet to start since Beye took charge on February 19 and is enduring a frustrating experience at Marseille. He has two goals and one assist in 11 appearances altogether, but his total of 412 minutes and just four starts in all competitions isn't what Nwaneri was hoping for.

‌



His status in the squad under Beye's management was made brutally obvious on Sunday, as he was left on the substitutes' bench. The Marseille boss made four changes, including to introduction fit-again Mason Greenwood, but Nwaneri remained unused.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ex-Arsenal star Aaron Ramsey sets incredible London Marathon time just weeks after retiring READ MORE :

Asked on L1+ why Nwaneri wasn't used, Beye had a stinging message for the youngster: "He’s a quality player, but he has to give us way more in his day-to-day commitment. Other players gave way more."

‌



What makes the situation even worse is that Marseille are currently short of attacking and creative options, with Hamed Traore, Igor Paixao, and Amine Gouiri all out injured. They have won just one of their last five games, yet Nwaneri remains on the periphery of Beye's thoughts.

When star forward Greenwood was out earlier this month, the Marseille boss was asked if Nwaneri might be the perfect replacement. His reply was telling.

"He (Nwaneri) is a big talent who needs to adapt to the intensity of Ligue 1," he said. "He looks like the ideal replacement for Mason but we have several quality players to choose from. He must understand he's come to a very, very high-level club."

‌



View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri has struggled on loan at Marseille (Image: Catherine Steenkeste, Getty Images)

Nwaneri's stock was much higher under De Zerbi's management. When fit, he started as a No.10 and showed what he can do by scoring 13 minutes into his debut in January. But the change of head coach, with De Zerbi joining Tottenham, has punctured his progress.

It comes in spite of there reportedly being a clause in his contract that sees the loan fee paid by Marseille rise the fewer minutes he plays. Marseille are, in effect, being charged more for keeping the England under-21 star on the bench.

‌



Nwaneri is therefore not getting the experience he thought he had signed up for. "The experience of seeing a big club like this, learning as much as possible, and being able to really add that to my skill set at the end of the season," he said upon arrival.

"When I came here, obviously I wasn't yet 100 per cent fit, but I'm working on it. I've also spoken with the staff and I think I'll be able to play more and more. I felt good during the last match. That's normal, of course, it's a process. There haven't been any injuries, so I feel good, honestly."

Sports.title: 11 players could be forced to sit out Man Utd vs Brentford as Michael Carrick gets timely boost
Sports.content:
11 players could be forced to sit out Man Utd vs Brentford as Michael Carrick gets timely boost

Manchester United host Brentford in the Premier League on Monday night, but a number of players on both sides will miss the match at Old Trafford through injury and suspension

View Image Michael Carrick has given an update on player fitness (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been handed a potential double injury boost ahead of their Premier League showdown with Brentford. The Red Devils welcome the Bees to Old Trafford on Monday night as they look to edge closer to sealing a Champions League berth.

‌



Michael Carrick's men currently sit third in the table, level on points with both Liverpool and Aston Villa in fourth and fifth respectively, though they hold a game in hand over both rivals.

‌



United edged past Chelsea 1-0 last weekend and will be keen to maintain that momentum when Brentford come to town. Ahead of the fixture, they will welcome back at least one central defensive option, with Harry Maguire returning from suspension.

‌



13 Man Utd players who could be moved on in savage summer clear-out READ MORE :

With the end-of-season run-in now well and truly underway, any absences through injury or suspension could prove decisive for both sides. Here's the latest on squad availability ahead of Monday night's crunch clash...

Manchester United

Leny Yoro was ruled out of the Chelsea victory after picking up a knock in training in the build-up to the match. Carrick has confirmed the young defender remains a doubt for the Brentford fixture.

"We're still working on [Leny]," he said, adding: "So, there's a possibility, there's a possibility, but at this stage, it's not 100 per cent sure."

‌



Full-back Patrick Dorgu remains unavailable for the fixture, though he is edging closer to a return to training. Carrick explained: "Patrick's working his way to being back.

"He's certainly making good progress and back closer to training with us, which is positive, so that's good news."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Defender Matthijs de Ligt has returned to the pitch as he continues his recuperation from a back injury, but it has been confirmed he will play no part in the match.

United will also be missing defender Lisandro Martinez , who serves a suspension following his red card against Leeds United earlier this month. On a brighter note, Maguire returns from his own ban and will be available for selection.

Brentford

The Bees head into the match with a number of injury concerns of their own. Keith Andrews has confirmed that Jordan Henderson, Rico Henry and Vitaly Janelt will all sit out, despite having returned to outdoor training as part of their respective recoveries.

‌



"They're doing well. I've just walked past all three of them, they've been doing a session separate from the group," he said.

"They're back on the grass and making good progress. They've all got slightly different timeframes as to when they'll be back, but they won't be available for Monday."

Midfielder Josh Dasilva and Kaye Furo will also be absent. Long-term casualties Fabio Carvalho and Antoni Milambo will likewise remain on the sidelines.
